Name: Liceu (Metro L3)
Tips: 08:30 - L2 from Sagrada Familia to Passeig de Gracia, change to L3, two stops to Liceu (~20 min). PICKPOCKET ALERT: L3, the Liceu platform and La Rambla are the densest pickpocket corridor in Spain. Bags in front from the escalator onward. No passports needed today.

Name: Granja La Pallaresa
Tips: 09:00 - the 1947 Petritxol granja institution. Order suissos (drinking chocolate thick enough to stand a spoon in, with whipped cream) and a plate of xurros to dip. Read the ceramic plaques set between shopfronts - they tell the street's history in tiles. Granja Dulcinea three doors down is the same institution if this is full.

Name: La Boqueria Market
Tips: 09:40, 20 min walk-through. Mon-Sat 08:00-20:30, CLOSED SUNDAYS - open on our Friday. IGNORE THE FRONT: the juice wall and fruit cups on La Rambla are theatre. Go deep to the fish hall at the back, the salt-cod stalls and the mushroom man. Buy nothing but a cone of jamon if a queue looks short.

Name: Basilica de Santa Maria del Pi
Tips: 10:00 at opening, 30-40 min. Mon-Sat 10:00-20:00. A single enormous nave with no aisles - Catalan Gothic at its purest - under one of the largest rose windows in the world (10 m across; current glass is a 1940s rebuild after a 1936 fire). BELL-TOWER CLIMBS RUN AT SET TIMES - ask at the desk when you buy. 50 m up a spiral, best cheap view in the Gothic Quarter.

Name: Sinagoga Major (El Call)
Tips: 10:45, ~30 min. Among the oldest surviving synagogue structures in Europe - two small rooms below street level, Roman foundations, a 10-min talk from whoever is on the desk. Look for the Hebrew inscription stone reset into the wall on C/ de Marlet. Barcelona's Call is the appetizer version of Girona's, which you get the next day.

Name: Plaça de Sant Felip Neri
Address: Plaça de Sant Felip Neri, 08002 Barcelona
Tips: 11:10 - go in quietly. The pockmarks across the church front are shrapnel from a January 1938 bombing that killed forty-two people, most of them children sheltering in the crypt. For decades it was said the marks were from firing squads; the truth is on the plaque now. A memorial before it is a photograph.

Name: Pont del Bisbe
Tips: 11:25, thirty seconds. The neo-Gothic bridge every guidebook cover uses - and it is from 1928, not the 15th century. Find the skull with a dagger through it carved on the underside, then move on before the tour groups re-form.

Name: Catedral de Barcelona (La Seu)
Address: Pla de la Seu s/n, 08002 Barcelona
Cost Range: 16 EUR; students under 25 14 EUR; rooftop tier ~19 EUR
Tips: 11:30, ~1 hr. THE FRIDAY DIVIDEND: Mon-Fri 09:30-18:30, where Saturday's tourist visit ends 17:15 and Sunday is worship-only 14:00-17:00. See in order: the crypt of Santa Eulalia (the city's 13-year-old co-patroness, alabaster sarcophagus under the high altar); the cloister with THIRTEEN WHITE GEESE, one for each year of her life; the 1519 Golden Fleece choir stalls; and the rooftop lift if the desk offers it. Shoulders and knees covered - enforced at the door.

Name: Temple d'August
Tips: 12:35, ~15 min, free, ~10:00-19:00. Four Corinthian columns 9 m tall from the 1st-century temple of Augustus, standing in a Gothic courtyard you would walk past ten times without noticing. A millstone in the doorway marks the summit of Mont Taber, the hill Barcelona was founded on - all 16.9 m of it.

Name: Plaça del Rei
Cost Range: Free to stand in (MUHBA interiors ~7 EUR)
Tips: 12:50 - the medieval royal courtyard with the fan-vaulted Salo del Tinell, where Ferdinand and Isabella reportedly received Columbus in 1493. Skip the MUHBA interiors today; the square is the sight. Then down C/ de la Ciutat past Plaça de Sant Jaume - Generalitat on one side, Ajuntament on the other, the same square the Romans put their forum in.

Name: Basilica de Santa Maria del Mar
Cost Range: 5 EUR cultural visit; 10 EUR with rooftop and towers
Tips: 13:15, ~40 min. Mon-Sat 10:00-18:00. THE SINGLE BEST THING OPTION B BUYS BACK. Built 1329-1383 - fifty-four years, one architect, one style - which is why it is the purest Catalan Gothic interior anywhere: three naves of near-equal height and octagonal columns set 13 m apart, the widest span of any medieval church in Europe. Funded and physically built by the parish; the bastaixos (port stevedores) carried the stone down from Montjuic on their backs and are carved into the bronze doors. Free during worship hours, but no rooftop and no explanation - the 5 EUR is the right 5 EUR.

Name: Bar del Pla
Tips: 14:00 - THE LUNCH PICK. Vaulted-brick tapas bar with a local crowd, two streets from the Picasso queue. Croquetes de pernil, patatas bravas, a glass of the house red. Mon-Thu 12:00-23:00, Fri-Sat to 24:00. Walk-in - arrive by 13:45 for the vault tables.

Name: Cal Pep
Tips: THE SPLURGE ALTERNATIVE to Bar del Pla. No menu, no choosing - you sit at the counter and Pep's team feeds you whatever the market gave them. FRIDAY 13:00-15:45 (closed Sundays). Queue from ~12:45; BAR ONLY, never the back room. WARNING: some years it shuts for three weeks in late August - call +34 933 10 79 61 the morning of.

Name: El Xampanyet
Tips: Lunch candidate, Tue-Sat 12:00-16:00. The 1929 cava-and-anchovies bodega - barrels, azulejo walls, joyful crush. Cantabrian anchovies and house xampanyet by the glass. WARNING: August break, reportedly back ~Aug 24-25 - confirm at the window before you queue. Standing only; don't wait for a stool. Directly opposite the Picasso Museum.

Name: Bar La Plata
Tips: THE GOTHIC-QUARTER ALTERNATIVE, a 6-min detour south. Open 1945, still serving the same four tapas: anchovies, pescaito frito, botifarra, tomato salad - wine poured from three barrels into small glasses. Standing, spilling onto the pavement, almost entirely locals. Mon-Sat 11:30-15:00, CLOSED SUNDAYS. CASH.

Name: Museu Picasso
Cost Range: 14 EUR online / 15 EUR door; 18-25: 7.50 EUR; under 18 free = 35.50 EUR for four
Tips: 15:30, ~1.5 hrs. BOOK A TIMED SLOT ONLINE - August afternoons sell out. FRIDAY 09:00-21:00 in summer, so nothing races you; air-conditioned, and the right place to be at the hottest hour. NOT the greatest hits - this is the Barcelona formation. The revelation is Ciencia i caritat, painted at FIFTEEN, hanging rooms away from the Blue Period portraits he made after Casagemas shot himself. Then the 58-canvas Les Menines series of 1957, a 75-year-old taking Velazquez apart frame by frame.

Name: El Born Centre de Cultura i Memoria
Tips: 17:00 - an entire 1700s neighbourhood, streets and drains and doorsteps, found intact under the floor of an iron market hall when they started digging for a library. Philip V razed it in 1714 to build the Ciutadella fortress; it lay under rubble for 300 years. You walk the gantry above it.

Name: Mercat de Santa Caterina
Tips: 17:00 alternative - where the neighbourhood actually shops, under Miralles's undulating ceramic wave roof (2005) in 325,000 coloured tiles. LOOK UP: the roof is the sight. Far fewer tourists than the Boqueria.

Name: Bar del Convent
Tips: Cold drink in a 17th-century convent cloister next door to the Born Centre - shaded, silent, no tourists. Tue-Sun.

Name: Parc de la Ciutadella
Tips: Optional 17:00 stop, 10 min east. The Cascada fountain that a student Gaudi worked on, and rowing boats on the lake - the cheap thrill if the teens have legs left. Daily 06:00-23:00.

Name: La Cova Fumada
Tips: 18:15 - THE SINGLE BEST REASON TO RUN OPTION B ON A FRIDAY. Open since 1944, NO SIGN on the door (look for brown shutters and a crowd), chalkboard menu, communal marble tables, CASH ONLY. The bomba was invented in this room. Order bombes, la raspa (fried anchovy spines, eaten whole), grilled sardines, chickpeas with morcilla. THE EVENING SERVICE IS THURSDAYS AND FRIDAYS ONLY, 18:00-20:00, and they close at 20:00 whether or not you have finished - be at the door at 18:15, not 19:30. Call +34 932 21 40 61 in the morning to check they are not on a summer holiday day. Backup 2 min away: Bar Jai-Ca.

Name: Barceloneta Beach
Address: Passeig Maritim de la Barceloneta, 08003 Barcelona
Tips: 19:15 - sand cooled, day-trippers gone, lifeguards on until ~19:30, sea ~24 C. Free showers on the boardwalk. ONE ADULT OWNS BAG-WATCH ON THE SAND AT ALL TIMES - prime pickpocket ground and phones left on towels vanish.

Name: Font de Carmen Amaya
Tips: 19:45, two minutes, free, a block back from the sand. A tiled fountain to the greatest bailaora of the 20th century, born in 1913 in the Somorrostro - the shanty-town that stood on this beach until 1966. Barcelona's whole claim on flamenco starts on this spot.

Name: Bar Jai-Ca
Tips: 20:45 - THE DINNER PICK, after sunset on the boardwalk (~20:31). The 1955 Barceloneta classic: bombas, la raspa, razor clams, calamari, cold beer, plastic-stool energy. Daily ~09:00-23:00. Also the standing backup if La Cova Fumada is shut.

Name: Bodega La Peninsular
Tips: Dinner alternative. High ceilings, marble tables, a chalkboard that changes with the catch - one of the few Barceloneta rooms still pointed at fresh fish rather than reheated tourist paella. Verify August hours.

Name: La Mar Salada
Address: Passeig de Joan de Borbo 58, 08003 Barcelona
Tips: Dinner alternative if you want the rice. Waterfront paella and market fish done properly - more intimate than 7 Portes and easier to get into. BOOK IN THE MORNING. WARNING: the front row of Pg. de Joan de Borbo is a tourist trap - laminated photo menus, 24 EUR frozen paella. If a man outside invites you in, keep walking.

Name: Palau Dalmases
Tips: OPTIONAL 21:30 - flamenco in the candlelit baroque salon of a 17th-century palace, ~70 seats, no stage, dancers within arm's reach. Three minutes from Santa Maria del Mar and opposite the Picasso, i.e. already on today's route, and the only evening this trip with room for it. Doing it means eating at Cova Fumada 18:15 plus a light bite in El Born, taking the beach earlier, and being seated by 21:15. Los Tarantos on Plaça Reial is the low-commitment version: 30 min, ~20 EUR, hourly from 19:30.

Name: Barceloneta (Metro L4)
Tips: 22:00 home - L4 from Barceloneta to Verdaguer (5 stops), change to L5, one stop to Sagrada Familia. ~20 min. Taxi or Bolt is 10-12 EUR if legs are done.
